title: WPMS/2911/2018 of ASSOCIATION OF COMBINED ENTRANCE EXAMINATION Vs UNION OF INDIA

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (M/S) No. 2911 of 2018
Association of Combined Entrance Examination .....Petitioner
Versus
Union of India and others. ....Respondents
Mr. Navneet Kaushik, Advocate for the petitioner.
There is no representation for the respondent no. 1.
Mr. S.R. Joshi, Standing Counsel with Mr. Vijay Khanduri, Brief Holder for the State
of Uttarakhand/ respondent no. 2.
Mr. Sanjay Bhatt, Advocate for respondent no. 3.
Mr. Ramji Srivastava, Advocate for respondent no. 4.
Dated: 26.02.2020
Hon'ble Manoj K. Tiwari, J. (Oral)
Heard learned counsel for the parties.
2. Petitioner is an association of private unaided educational
institutions in Uttarakhand. Members of the petitioner association are
running Ayurvedic Colleges, which are conducting various courses in
Ayurvedic Medicine including BAMS course.
3. Petitioner is aggrieved by the order dated 18.09.2018
passed by Government of Uttarakhand, whereby petitioner's
representation challenging the requirement of admission to BAMS
course through merit list of NEET examination, was rejected.
4. A perusal of the said order indicates that it has been passed
in view of the directions issued by the Central Government to admit
students in Ayurvedic, Homeopathic and Unani Colleges on the basis
of their score in NEET examination conducted by the Central Board of
Secondary Education (for short 'CBSE'). Letters issued by the Central
Government on 26.04.2017, 11.06.2018, 05.06.2018 and 23.01.2018
have been relied in the impugned order.

2
5. Contention of the petitioner in the writ petition is that
NEET examination conducted by CBSE is referable to Section 10-D of
the Indian Medical Council Act and there is no analogous provision in
Indian Medicines Central Council Act, 1970, therefore, the requirement
of passing NEET examination cannot be applied in respect of
Ayurvedic and Homeopathic Medical courses. He further submits that
NEET examination is held for admission to MBBS and BDS courses
alone and it was never intended to apply for admission to Ayurvedic
Medical courses.
6. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that similar
issue was raised by Ayurvedic and Homeopathic Medical Colleges
before various High Courts in which directions were issued to permit
admissions in Ayurvedic and Homeopathic colleges on the basis of the
marks scored by the students in the qualifying examination, without
reference to the marks scored by them in the NEET UG-2018. In
support of this contention, learned counsel for the petitioner has cited
one judgment rendered by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Civil Appeal No.
1393 of 2019 (Association of Managements of Homeopathic Medical
Colleges of Maharashtra v. Union of India and Ors.). Paragraphs 5 & 6
of the said judgment, which have been relied by learned counsel for the
petitioner are extracted below:-
"5. We have perused the judgments and orders passed by the High
Courts of Patna , Karnataka, Madras, Rajasthan, Punjab & Haryana,
Allahabad and Kolkata. Directions were issued in favour of the
students permitting admissions on the basis of the marks in the
qualifying examination without reference to the marks secured by
them in the NEET UG-2018 examination. The learned Additional
Solicitor General fairly submitted that none of the judgments or
orders passed by the High Courts have been challenged.
6. Though the last date for admission to the BHMS course was 15th
November, 2018, we are informed that the last date was extended till
20th December, 2018 by the Allahabad High Court. Though there is
no agreement on the exact number of vacant seats, it is common
ground that there are vacant seats for admission to the 1st year
BHMS course in the State of Maharashtra. As there is no uniformity
in the matter of admission to the 1st year BHMS course for the year
2018-19, as securing minimum marks in NEET is not required in
some States pursuant to orders of the High Courts, we are of the
opinion that the Appellants are entitled to the relief of admissions
being made without reference to the letter dated 11th June, 2018 of
Respondent No.1 and the consequential notice of Respondent No.3.

3
In other words, the Appellant-Association should be permitted to
make admissions to the 1st year BHMS course for the academic
session 2018-19 on the basis of the eligibility criteria mentioned in
the information brochure dated 5th February, 2018. A candidate who
has secured minimum marks in the NEET UG-2018 shall be eligible
for admission to the 1st year BHMS course for the academic year
2018-19
7. However, Hon'ble Supreme Court in Civil Appeal No.
603 of 2020 (Union of India v. Federation of Self-Financed Ayurvedic
Colleges Punjab & Ors) has expressed agreement with the submissions
made by Central Council of Indian Medicine and Union of India that
minimum standards cannot be lowered even for admission to AYUSH
courses. It was further held that non-availability of eligible candidates
for admission to AYUSH under graduate courses cannot be a reason to
lower the standards prescribed by the Central Council for admission.
8. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that he is not
pressing the reliefs, as sought in the writ petition, in view of the
notification issued by Central Council of Indian Medicine and the
verdict given by Hon'ble Supreme Court that NEET would be
necessary even for admission to Ayurvedic Medical courses. He,
however, submits that different Ayurvedic Colleges, which are member
of petitioner association have granted admission to eligible candidates
during academic session 2018-19 on the strength of interim order dated
14.11.2018 passed in this writ petition, therefore, interest of such
students may be protected or else they would lose two precious years of
their study. Relevant extract of the interim order passed by this Court
on 14.11.2018 is reproduced below for ready reference:
"4. The respondent Union of India in its counter affidavit has also
relied upon the interim order of Karnataka High Court, which says
that in case the list of NEET qualified candidates has been
exhausted, then admission can be given to such candidates who had
not appeared for NEET examination, but have the minimum
qualification to undergo the AYUSH courses.
5. In view of the facts of the case and in view of the interim order
passed by the Karnataka High Court, on which reliance has been
placed by none else but the Union of India, as an interim measure it
is directed that the State Government shall consider giving
admission in the petitioner colleges in the light of the interim order
passed by the Karnataka High Court. This is being done so that any
admission being made in the petitioner association should be under

4
the overall supervision and control of the State Government, or
through a committee appointed by it. Let the admission be done in
accordance with law."
9. A perusal of the aforesaid interim order reveals that it was
passed in the light of the stand taken by Union of India in its counter
affidavit that Hon'ble Karnataka High Court has passed an interim
order, which provides that in case the list of NEET qualified candidates
has been exhausted, then admission can be given to such candidates
who had not appeared for NEET examination, but have the minimum
qualification to undergo the AYUSH courses. It further reveals that
admissions were to be given under overall supervision and control of
the State Government or through a committee appointed by it, but not
unilaterally by the Ayurvedic colleges.
10. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that pursuant to
the interim order, Uttarakhand Ayurvedic University held counseling at
Dehradun on 15.11.2018 and students were admitted in different
Ayurvedic colleges through said counseling. He further submits that
due to peculiar geographical condition of State of Uttarakhand, some
candidates residing in far off places in State of Uttarakhand could not
reach Dehradun in time so as to appear before the counseling board,
consequently, some students were admitted by the Ayurvedic colleges
concerned without reference to the counseling board constituted by
Uttarakhand Ayurvedic University. He, however, submits that all such
students fulfilled the minimum eligibility criteria and all of them had
secured more than 50% marks in qualifying examination i.e. 12th
standard. He further submits that petitioner tenders unconditional
apology for this mistake on the part of the Ayurvedic colleges
concerned.
11. Uttarakhand Ayurvedic University is the affiliating
University in respect of all Ayurvedic colleges, which are members of
petitioner association.

5
12. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the said
University has enrolled all the students, who were given admission
through State counseling held by Uttarakhand Ayurvedic University,
however, students who were given admission directly without
counseling have not been enrolled by the University. He, therefore,
submits that the University be directed to enroll such students also, who
were admitted by the concerned Ayurvedic colleges without State
counseling.
13. This Court vide orders dated 06.12.2019 and 06.01.2020
had asked the University to examine whether the students admitted by
the Ayurvedic colleges fulfill all the eligibility criteria for such
admission.
14. Mr. Sanjay Bhatt, learned counsel appearing for the
University submits that the University has enrolled all the students who
were admitted in different colleges through counseling held by the
University on 15.11.2018, however, the University has not enrolled
such students who have been given admission without reference to the
counseling Board. However, he admits that the students who were
admitted without State counseling were also granted admission on or
before the deadline fixed for the purpose i.e. 15.11.2018.
15. Since the University has enrolled all students who were
admitted through State counseling held by the University, therefore, no
grievance of the petitioner subsists as regards such students. The only
grievance which remains is regarding such students who were admitted
by members of the petitioner association without State counseling.
16. Pursuant to the orders dated 06.12.2019 and 06.01.2020
passed by this Court, Uttarakhand Ayurvedic University has collected
information regarding the students who were given admission without
State counseling and it is compiled in tabular form, which has been
produced in Court today by Mr. Sanjay Bhatt, learned counsel for the
University. Mr. Sanjay Bhatt submits that number of students admitted

6
in different Ayurvedic colleges without State counseling is different.
He further submits that the University has verified the educational
certificates of all these students and it was found that all these students
fulfilled the minimum eligibility requirement for admission to BAMS
course, as all of them have passed the qualifying examination with
more than 50% marks. Mr. Bhatt has also produced in Court one letter
dated 25.11.2019, which is made part of the record. Based on the said
letter, Mr. Bhatt submits that the University is ready to consider such
students for enrollment, who were directly admitted by the Ayurvedic
colleges without State counseling, keeping in view their future.
17. Mr. Sanjay Bhatt, learned counsel for the University has
informed that as many as 474 students have been admitted in BAMS
course without State counseling in different colleges during academic
year 2018-19, who are yet to be enrolled by the University.
18. Mr. Ramji Srivastava, learned counsel appearing for
respondent no. 4 submits that the concerned Ayurvedic Colleges had
granted admissions without State counseling in defiance of the interim
order passed by this Court, therefore, the University had rightly refused
to enroll such students. He, however, concedes that such students were
also admitted before the deadline fixed i.e. 15.11.2018. He further
submits that his client has no objection if students who possess the
requisite educational qualification and have passed the qualifying
examination with more than 50% marks are enrolled by the University.
19. Mr. S.R. Joshi, learned Standing Counsel appearing for the
State submits that State Government had passed the order dated
18.09.2018 in view of directions issued by the Central Government
from time to time and the State Government has nothing more to say in
the matter.
20. Although, 474 students were given admission directly in
the year 2018 without State counseling by the concerned Ayurvedic
colleges in disregard of the interim order of this Court, however, this

7
Court is of the opinion that since the students are not at fault, therefore,
their future cannot be jeopardized for a mistake committed by the
concerned Ayurvedic colleges.
21. As stated earlier, Uttarakhand Ayurvedic University has
expressed its readiness to consider these 474 students for enrollment so
that they may take the examination conducted by the University. The
University after verification of the educational certificates of these 747
students has made statement through its counsel that all these students
are otherwise eligible for admission to BAMS course.
22. Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Union of India v.
Federation of Self-Financed Ayurvedic Colleges Punjab & others in
Civil Appeal No. 603 of 2020 has permitted such students to continue
their studies who were granted admission on the strength of interim
orders passed by the High Courts. Relevant extract of para 12 of the
aforesaid judgment is reproduced below:-
"However, in view of admission of a large number of students to the
AYUSH Under Graduate courses for the year 2019-2020 on the
strength of interim orders passed by the High Courts, we direct that
the students may be permitted to continue provided that they were
admitted prior to the last date of admission i.e. 15th October, 2019.
The said direction is also applicable to students admitted to Post
Graduate courses before 31st October, 2019. This is a one-time
exercise which is permitted in view of the peculiar circumstances.
Therefore, this order shall not be treated as a precedent."
23. Having regard to the peculiar facts and circumstances of
the case and particularly with a view to protect the interest of the
students who are pursuing their study for the last more than one year in
the concerned colleges, this Court thinks that ends of justice would be
met if the University is directed to consider the case of these 474
students for enrolment, if they are otherwise found eligible.
24. Since the members of the petitioner association have
flouted the order of this Court by directly admitting such students
without State counseling, therefore, the petitioner association will have
pay ` 50,00,000/- as penalty to the University. The University shall

8
consider the case of such students who were admitted without State
counseling, for enrollment.
25. In such view of the matter, the writ petition is disposed of
with a direction to the petitioner to deposit a sum of ` 50,00,000/- as
penalty with the Uttarakhand Ayurvedic University on or before
05.03.2020. The University shall consider grant of enrollment to these
474 students who were admitted directly without reference to the State
counseling in accordance with law. It is made clear that the burden of
penalty shall be borne by management of the concerned Ayurvedic
colleges, which shall not be shifted to any of the students. The
University shall be at liberty to move an appropriate application before
this Court, in case petitioner fails to deposit the amount of penalty.
26. Let a certified copy of this order be issued to the parties
within 24 hours.
 (Manoj K. Tiwari, J) 26.02.2020
Navin
